scope: Authorised renv cache-link backup repair and successful production rerun; no scientific edits owned

attempts.outcome: stopped safely on concurrent source drift during hashing

independent_code_review.scope: Approved renv package-leaf symlinks and existing snapshot integrity and retention safeguards; no general symlink support.
observations: All 31 live checkout links were under models/pilot-asr/renv/library, targeted the expected v5 cache path and matched package versions in that project lockfile.
The patch records literal link targets and source link signatures separately; destination link identities omit device and ctime; source and destination symlink modes are not directly compared.
Manifest validation rejects a link that is a parent of another manifest path. Sample and full restore include links and their project lockfiles.

Old manifests, source inventories and identity receipts default missing symlink maps to empty. Code inspection supports legacy compatibility; the current legacy regression does not remove every newly introduced symlink key.
External cache bytes are deliberately not backed up; the receipts disclose this.
git diff --check passed. The parent is running the regression suite; this review did not independently run it or touch production.
Delta review: the parent reports the 28-test suite is running; this agent did not run the suite or access production. git diff --check passed.

Final delta review found no outstanding material issue in the approved renv leaf-link and backup-integrity scope. Retained generations are private and read-only by permissions, not WORM; capture is not a project-wide atomic snapshot. git diff --check passed. Parent reruns the suite; production was not accessed by this reviewer.

findings.scenario: A directory recorded as ordinary in a generation is replaced with a symlink after verify_metadata and before shutil.copy2 reads a descendant. copy2 follows ancestor symlinks and can read and copy external cache bytes before the checksum check. If the external file has the expected bytes, the check may also pass.
findings.qualification: Completed generations are normally sealed; this requires concurrent modification of a generation and is not the normal steady-state path.
findings.recommendation: Copy restore input through the descriptor-relative regular_file helper, with no-follow traversal and opened-file identity/stability checking; add a race regression that swaps an ancestor immediately before restore copying.

findings.scenario: seal checks p.is_symlink and then separately calls p.stat/p.chmod. A file or directory component swapped to a symlink between those calls can cause chmod on a target outside the generation. The topdown=False directory pass also chmods by pathname.
findings.qualification: This requires a concurrent mutation while sealing; ordinary stable renv leaf links are skipped and are not chmodded.
findings.recommendation: Use directory_fd and fchmod on verified directory descriptors, and regular_file plus fchmod on verified file descriptors; skip approved symlink entries without following their targets. Add a link-swap-before-chmod regression.

findings.scenario: inventory closes its safe directory fd after listdir, then calls path.lstat and os.readlink on pathnames. A concurrent replacement of the parent directory by a symlink can make those metadata lookups follow that ancestor. Later safe signature/file reads generally stop the capture, but an absolute no-target-dereference claim is not yet established.
findings.recommendation: Keep the verified directory descriptor open while doing os.stat(name, dir_fd=descriptor, follow_symlinks=False) and os.readlink(name, dir_fd=descriptor); test concurrent replacement of a package parent.

findings.scenario: seal unconditionally fchmods every regular inode. Unchanged files are hardlinked to prior generations, so even setting an unchanged mode changes their shared inode ctime and violates the existing no-op chmod safeguard.
findings.recommendation: After fstat, call fchmod only if mode has write bits; test by spying on fchmod for an already-readonly inherited inode. Whole-run ctime comparisons are unsuitable because hardlink creation itself can change ctime.

findings.scenario: directory_fd catches OSError thrown by its with-body; a missing final lockfile in path_stat is converted from FileNotFoundError to RuntimeError. check_renv_lock cannot catch it as intended, so the missing-lock regression and diagnostic fail. Reproduced with a nonexistent name in /private/tmp.
findings.recommendation: Restrict the OSError handler to directory-component opens; do not wrap exceptions raised by the caller inside the yielded context.

resolved_findings.resolution: restore now reads input through descriptor-relative regular_file with O_NOFOLLOW
seal now uses no-follow directory/file descriptors and fchmod; known manifest symlinks are matched and skipped
inventory now uses path_stat and link_target, both of which resolve parent components using directory_fd and O_NOFOLLOW
seal checks current descriptor mode and calls fchmod only when write bits are set; the zero-change incremental test spies on fchmod
directory_fd now confines OSError wrapping to opening directory components; path_stat on a missing final entry was independently confirmed to raise FileNotFoundError

restore_requirement: Literal package-cache links and renv.lock are preserved; rebuild packages using renv::restore when the Mac cache is unavailable. No guarantee of future external package source availability.
schedule: Daily incremental; full scrub automatically when seven days have elapsed since last successful scrub. No scheduling or retention changes.
